newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Horse racing-Facts and figures about Melbourne Cup.
newsitem.headline: Horse racing-Facts and figures about Melbourne Cup.

text.p: Factfile on the Melbourne Cup horse race, Australia's premier handicap, to be held at Flemington race course on Tuesday:
Total prize money is A$2.2 million ($1.74 million). Winner gets A$1.43 million, A$440,000 for second, A$198,000 for third, A$88,000 for fourth, and $44,000 for fifth.
The race was first run at Flemington in 1861. It is normally run on the first Tuesday in November, which is a public holiday in Victoria state.
A field limit of 24 horses was introduced in 1969. The largest field in Cup history was in 1890, when Carbine won carrying 66 kg (145 pounds) -- the highest winning weight on record.
The smallest field was in 1863 when there were seven starters. Banker won with 34 kg (74 pounds) -- the lowest winning weight on record.
The race was run over a distance of two miles until 1972, when it began to be measured in metric terms at 3,200 metres, shortening the course by a distance of 61-1/2 feet (18.75 metres).
Race record over two miles: 3 mins 19.1 seconds by Rain Lover in 1968.
Race record over 3,200 metres: 3:16.3 by Kingston Rule in 1990.
First horse bred and trained outside Australasia to win the race: Irish raider Vintage Crop in 1993.
This year's favourite: Irish raider Oscar Schindler at 3-1. Last year's winner Doriemus is third favourite at 7-1.
